concept.name: Abandoned baby
concept.definition: A rare three-candlestick reversal pattern similar to a morning/evening doji star but stricter: the middle doji must gap away from both neighboring candles such that its shadows do not overlap theirs at either side. The bullish version (doji gapped below between a black and a white candle) and bearish version (doji gapped above between a white and a black candle) are read as major reversal signals.
concept.intuition: A lone doji sits isolated on the chart with empty space on both sides, like an abandoned baby; the market gapped away from the trend, froze, and then gapped back the opposite way.
concept.mechanics: Bullish form: long black candle, then a doji whose high is below the prior candle's low, then a white candle whose low is above the doji's high. Bearish form mirrors this with gaps above. Because it requires two full shadow gaps around a doji, it is extremely rare: multi-decade S&P 500 scans find only a handful of occurrences.
concept.formula: Bullish abandoned baby when H2 < L1 (doji = candle 2) and L3 > H2; bearish when L2 > H1 and H3 < L2.
concept.failure_modes: Its rarity makes it almost unusable in practice and prevents meaningful statistical validation; tiny samples give unreliable efficiency estimates. In gapless 24-hour markets genuine instances are nearly nonexistent, and relaxed matches degrade into ordinary doji stars.
concept.misconceptions: It is not just a morning or evening doji star: the doji's entire shadow range must be separated by gaps from both neighbors, not merely its body. Its textbook rarity also means most chart 'sightings' do not meet the strict definition.
concept.example: A stock in a downtrend prints a long black candle (low 28.00), then a doji trading entirely between 27.20 and 27.60, then a white candle whose low is 27.80 and which closes at 29.50. The fully gapped doji makes this a bullish abandoned baby rather than a morning doji star.
